lead: Wipers clear the screen with a small permanent-magnet motor that has two speeds and a park switch; a washer pump and a rain sensor look after the rest. Keyless entry is a short radio conversation between a fob and the car, and the immobiliser is a second, stricter conversation that decides whether the engine may fire at all. These are the body electronics a driver touches every day: the blade that returns to the bottom of the glass, the door that unlocks as the handle is pulled, and the engine that stays silent for the wrong key.
prereq: You need Unit 1 for the battery and starting circuit, and Chapter 2.1 for what a spark needs; body-network frames are in Unit 6.

sections.h3: The wiper motor, its brushes and the park switch

blocks.text: A windscreen wiper is a permanent-magnet DC motor turning a crank. The field does not come from a winding: two curved ferrite magnets in the body give a steady flux. The armature carries the windings, and current reaches them through carbon brushes pressing on a commutator. A worm gearbox cuts the motor's few thousand rev/min to about 40 to 60 sweeps per minute at the blade, and a crank-and-link mechanism turns rotation into the back-and-forth arc.

Most wiper motors have three brushes. Two are the normal supply and earth. The third sits about 30° away and feeds the armature at a shifted angle, which distorts the field and weakens the flux per pole. A weaker field lets the armature spin faster at the same 12 V. So one brush pair gives low speed and the third brush gives high speed — the speed change comes from brush position, not from a higher voltage.
The park switch stops the blade at the bottom of the glass. It is a cam-driven contact inside the gearbox, not the stalk switch the driver moves.

items: Driver switches the stalk off; the direct supply to the motor is removed.
A second path through the park-switch contact keeps the motor running.
The cam holds that contact closed over most of the circle.
At the park notch the contact opens and the supply is gone.
The switch then shorts the armature to earth, braking it so the blade cannot coast past the bottom.

sections.h3: Intermittent wipe, washer pump and rain sensor

blocks.text: Light rain does not need continuous wiping. The intermittent relay powers the motor for one wipe, waits, then repeats. The wait is set by an RC timer: a capacitor charges through a resistor until its voltage crosses a threshold; the relay then fires and the capacitor resets. A potentiometer on the stalk varies the resistance, so the driver picks the delay. A wiper ECU does the same job with a counter in software.

blocks.where: T is the delay in seconds, R is the timing resistance in ohms, C is the timing capacitance in farads. R = 100 kΩ with C = 100 µF gives T = 100 000 × 0.0001 = 10 s.

blocks.text: The washer pump is a small permanent-magnet motor driving a centrifugal impeller, drawing 2 to 5 A for a second or two. A wipe-after-wash timer runs the blades two or three strokes after the pump stops, so the fluid is spread and then cleared.

A rain sensor shines infrared light into the glass at an angle. The light normally reflects inside the glass by total internal reflection and comes back to a photodiode. Water on the outside lets some light escape, so the photodiode current falls; the electronics read that as rain and step through intermittent, low and high speed.

sections.h3: Remote entry, passive entry and the immobiliser

blocks.text: Remote keyless entry (RKE) is a one-way radio link. Pressing the fob sends a frame: a serial number identifying the fob, a command (lock, unlock, boot) and a rolling code. The receiver, usually in the body control module, demodulates the frame at 315 MHz or 433 MHz and passes it on.

A fixed code can be recorded and replayed by a thief. A rolling code changes on every press: fob and receiver hold the same counter and the same secret key, and the transmitted number is a keyed hash of the counter. The receiver accepts a few values ahead of its own counter, so a fob pressed by accident out of range still works; beyond that window the two are out of step and the fob must be resynchronised.

Passive keyless entry removes the button. Aerials in the door handles and cabin transmit a low-frequency wake-up, about 125 kHz. The fob answers on UHF with its identity. If the answer is valid and the fob is outside the car, the door unlocks when the handle is touched; if the fob is inside, the start button is allowed.

The immobiliser is a second, stricter check. The key holds a transponder — a glass capsule with a chip and a coil, no battery. A coil around the lock barrel drives 125 kHz into it and powers the chip by induction. The car sends a challenge; the chip computes a response with its secret key and returns it. On a match the immobiliser ECU sends a start enable to the engine ECU over the bus. Without it the engine ECU will not drive the coils or open the injectors: the engine cranks but never fires.
Central locking motors do the lock and unlock work that the RKE frame commands, driven by the body control module after a valid frame.

figure.caption: The receiver validates the RKE frame and advances the rolling counter on each valid press; the immobiliser ECU separately runs the transponder challenge and alone issues the start enable.

spec.aria: Sequence diagram with two parts. Remote keyless entry: the key fob sends a rolling code and ID to the receiver, which advances its counter and drives the door lock actuator to unlock. Immobiliser: the immobiliser ECU powers the key transponder on a 125 kHz coil and sends a challenge, the transponder returns a response, the immobiliser ECU sends a start enable to the engine ECU, and the engine ECU reports cranking and firing status back.

examples.question: A wiper arm is 500 mm long from pivot to tip and sweeps through 120°. It completes 45 wipes per minute, where one wipe is one out-and-back sweep. The intermittent relay times its delay with a 100 kΩ resistor and a 100 µF capacitor. Find (a) the average speed of the wiper tip and (b) the intermittent delay.
steps: Convert the sweep angle to radians: θ = 120 × π/180 = 2.094 rad.
Arc travelled in one one-way sweep: s = rθ = 0.500 m × 2.094 = 1.047 m.
One wipe is out and back: 2 × 1.047 = 2.094 m.
Average tip speed = 0.75 s⁻¹ × 2.094 m = 1.5708 m/s. The instantaneous tip speed is not constant: it is zero at the ends of the arc and peaks near mid-sweep at about 1.6 times the average.
examples.answer: The average tip speed is 1.5708 m/s (about 1.57 m/s), with the instantaneous speed peaking near mid-sweep at about 2.5 m/s, and the intermittent delay is 10.0 s.
examples.check:
import math

r = 0.500            # arm length, m
theta = math.radians(120)
arc = r * theta      # one-way arc, m
wipe = 2 * arc       # out and back, m
rate = 45 / 60       # wipes per second
v = rate * wipe      # tip speed, m/s

R = 100e3            # ohm
C = 100e-6           # farad
T = R * C            # seconds

print(round(v, 4))
print(round(T, 4))

examples.question: A rain sensor's photodiode delivers 5.0 µA when the glass is dry and 2.0 µA when it is wet. The sense resistor is 100 kΩ. Find the change in the voltage seen by the comparator.
steps: Dry voltage: V = I × R = 5.0 × 10⁻⁶ A × 100 000 Ω = 0.50 V.
Wet voltage: V = I × R = 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ A × 100 000 Ω = 0.20 V.
examples.answer: The comparator input falls by 0.30 V when rain lands on the glass.
examples.check:
R = 100e3
v_dry = 5.0e-6 * R
v_wet = 2.0e-6 * R
print(round(v_dry - v_wet, 4))

traps: The immobiliser usually does not cut the starter. It stops the spark and the injectors, so the engine cranks normally and never fires.
A rolling code out of step fails even with the correct key: many presses far from the car push the fob counter past the receiver's acceptance window.
Wiper high speed comes from the third brush position, not from 24 V or a bigger motor; the supply stays 12 V.
RC delay comes out in seconds only with R in ohms and C in farads: 100 kΩ with 100 µF is 10 s, not 10 ms.
The park switch is inside the gearbox cam, not the stalk switch the driver moves — examiners ask for both.

quiz.q: What is the job of the park switch in a wiper motor?
quiz.a: It keeps the motor supplied through a cam contact until the blade reaches the bottom notch, then opens and brakes the armature so the blade stops in the park position.

quiz.q: Explain why a third brush gives a higher wiper speed.
quiz.a: The third brush feeds armature current at a shifted angle, which weakens the flux per pole. A weaker field raises the speed at the same applied voltage, so no extra supply is needed.

quiz.q: A wiper arm is 0.6 m long and sweeps 90° at 30 wipes per minute, one wipe being out and back. Find the average tip speed.
quiz.a: 90° = 1.571 rad; arc = 0.6 × 1.571 = 0.9425 m; one wipe = 1.885 m; rate = 0.5 wipes/s; average tip speed = 0.9425 m/s, with the instantaneous speed peaking near mid-sweep at about 1.6 times this value.

quiz.q: An intermittent wiper timer uses 47 kΩ and 220 µF. Find the delay.
A car with the correct key cranks but does not fire. Give two faults consistent with this.
quiz.a: The coil around the lock barrel is open, so the transponder is never powered; or the immobiliser ECU is not sending the start enable, for example after a bus fault or an unmatched key. Either way spark and injection stay disabled.

quiz.q: How does passive keyless entry differ from remote keyless entry?
quiz.a: RKE needs a button press on a one-way UHF link. PKE wakes the fob with a low-frequency aerial in the car, the fob replies on UHF, and the door unlocks on touching the handle; starting is allowed if the fob is inside.

quiz.q: Why is a rolling code safer than a fixed code?
quiz.a: A recorded fixed code can be replayed later. A rolling code is a keyed hash of a counter, so an old recording is behind the receiver's counter and is rejected.

beyond: Not for the exam. Production wipers now sit on the LIN bus, so the body controller sends a speed or a delay and the motor module does the rest. Phone-as-key systems replace the UHF fob with Bluetooth Low Energy or ultra-wideband ranging, which measures distance so a relay attack fails. Immobiliser functions live inside larger secure elements and are developed to ISO 26262 and AUTOSAR requirements. Search terms: LIN wiper module, UWB digital key, challenge-response transponder, rolling code resynchronisation.
